description.narrative: The project will improve the employability of graduates from technical and vocational education and training (TVET) programs and courses in three priority sectors of the economy in Mongolia: agriculture, construction, and road and transportation. The project, which has several innovative features, will (i) develop an industry-driven TVET system; (ii) upgrade selected TVET providers to implement competency-based training and assessment; (iii) establish training systems for TVET teachers and managers; (iv) support secondary education career guidance and schools that specialize in technology; and (v) establish an effective project management system.

description.narrative: Enhanced responsiveness of the TVET system to labor market demand in the three priority sectors.

15,500 students have obtained completion certificates of CBT programs and courses for the key occupations in the priority sectors developed in collaboration with employers, and industry and professional associations, of which 2,800 (18.1%) are female students (2012 baseline: 14.8%) Achievement: 6529 Progress/Status: Achieved. TVET standards and CBT curriculum for 15 occupations in 3 priority sectors were approved by the order No. A/303 of the Minister of Labor and Social Protection in September 2019 and delivered to TVET providers for implementation. According to the VET AIMC survey, 237 TVET teachers delivered courses for 14 occupations in 2019-2020 school year. In the academic year of 2019-2020, in total 6,529 students graduated from the studies in the priority sectors at the TVET institutions (3,197 in construction, 2,022 in road and transport, and 1,310 in agriculture). In total, 8,718 (4,574 in construction, 2,744 in road and transport, and 1,399 in agriculture) students enrolled the priority sector studies in the academic year 2020-2021. Hence, it is expected that by the project closing, there would be 15,247 students who would have completed CBT programs in the priority sectors. Data Source: MLSP reports; reports of the selected TVET providers

3,000 students certified in the key occupations at the assessment and certification centers Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Achieved. The three assessment centers have been established, but it has not started doing the assessment and certification due to the COVID-19 restrictions and lockdown. It was expected that assessment and certification in the key occupations would start in July 2021. Data Source: MLSP reports; reports of assessment and certification centers

Eighth and ninth grade students in all schools have gender-sensitive career guidance integrated with national instructional plan Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Achieved ahead of time and exceeded the target. Since 2016, all eighth and ninth grade students have been enrolled in career guidance programs. Since 2018, 10th-12th grade students have also started receiving learning and career guidance. Data Source: MES reports; M&E reports Base year: 2012 Baseline value: N

Output: 2. Selected TVET providers upgraded to implement CBT&A in the three priority sectors. Indicator: 170 teachers of the selected TVET providers trained in TVS for the key occupations by 2021 Achievement: 181 Progress/Status: Achieved. The CBT pedagogy and assessment training for the TVET teachers was organized for 181 TVET teachers and staff members (63 female) on 6-10 May and 13-17 May 2019, respectively. The TVS training programs and cost estimates for the cascade training for TVET teachers of 13 occupations were developed and submitted to MLSP for approval. The short-term trainings are planned to be delivered in summer 2021 for 146 teachers for the key occupations through the assessment and certification centers and industries. Data Source: MLSP reports; reports of the selected TVET providers; M&E reports

Output: 2. Selected TVET providers upgraded to implement CBT&A in the three priority sectors. Indicator: 20 selected TVET providers with upgraded equipment and facilities offering CBT programs and courses for the key occupations in the priority sectors by 2021 Achievement: 11 Progress/Status: Being achieved. The Sukhbaatar aimag TVET provider was excluded from an initial list of 20 due to the lack of qualitative proposal, by the order of MLSP minister. Hence, in total 19 TVET providers are planned to be upgraded under the project. Out of selected 19 selected TVET providers, the upgrading of eight have been completed, 3 have been physically completed and are under the warranty period while upgrading of 8 TVET providers are going. It is expected that all the upgrading will be completed by August 2021. Data Source: MLSP reports; reports of the selected TVET providers; M&E reports

Output: 2. Selected TVET providers upgraded to implement CBT&A in the three priority sectors. Indicator: 30 managers of the selected TVET providers trained in industry-driven TVET management by 2018 Achievement: 53 Progress/Status: Achieved. A 2-stage training for TVET managers took place in February and June 2019 for 53 principals including 24 (44%) women from 36 TVET providers: (i) training conducted on February 2019; and (ii) training for the training managers conducted on 17-18 June 2019, delivered by the University of Finance and Economics. MLSP and TVET AIMC decided to organize a follow-up training for the TVET training managers and methodologists, a subject to COVID-19 situation. Specifically, the training on industry-driven TVET management and CBT methodology will be provided for 86 persons (78 training managers and methodologists of 39 public TVET schools and 4 regional methodology centers (RMC). The training program and schedule were submitted to MLSP and VET AIMC for approval. Data Source: MLSP reports

Output: 2. Selected TVET providers upgraded to implement CBT&A in the three priority sectors. Indicator: 350 students completed internship for key occupations in the priority sectors by 2021 Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Not achieved. Internships of students at the selected TVET providers, following the CBT curriculum, was expected to start in 2021. Due to COVID-19 related restrictions in 2020, no industry-based internship training was organized for TVET students due to delays in the project implementation and external factors like pandemic. Data Source: MLSP reports; reports of the selected TVET providers; M&E reports

Output: 2. Selected TVET providers upgraded to implement CBT&A in the three priority sectors. Indicator: 50 teachers of the selected TVET providers trained in TVS for the key occupations through industry placement by 2021 Achievement: 49 Progress/Status: Achieved. 49 (25 female) teachers of the selected TVET providers, including 3 ACCs, were trained through industry placement as Master Trainers for 15 key occupations on 6-31 May 2019. Training was delivered by the training teams of professional associations, industry and university professors. However, only 30 of the master trainers remain at their positions as of May 2021. Data Source: MLSP reports; reports of the selected TVET providers; M&E reports

Indicator: 30 master TVS trainers identified and trained Achievement: 38 Progress/Status: Achieved. In total 38 master trainers (28 women) for the CBT pedagogy and assessment completed 120-hour training program in March 2019, which was delivered in cooperation with industry associations and employers. Data Source: MLSP reports; M&E reports
Output: 3. Training systems for TVET managers and teachers established in the three priority sectors. Indicator: of which about 5 are female Achievement: 28 Data Source: MLSP reports; M&E reports

Output: 4. Secondary education career guidance and advanced elective courses in science, technology, engineering, and math supported. Indicator: 30 senior secondary schools equipped to offer advanced elective courses in STEM subjects Achievement: 555 Progress/Status: Achieved. In total 6 person/months of international and 28 person/months of national consultancy services were engaged by the project to support the implementation of senior secondary STEM education curriculum in 2016-2020. The science, technology, engineering and math (STEM) education training modules were developed in 2016 for 10th grade and in 2018 for 12th grade; and delivered as materials for trainings organized under the project; and are being used as training tools in all schools nationwide. Senior secondary design and technology, math, chemistry, and physics teachers were trained in the new curriculum in 2016, 2018 and 2019. In total, in duplicated numbers 14,089 STEM subject teachers from all senior secondary schools attended nationwide training sessions in three years. Moreover, more than 600 TVET teachers participated in STEM subject training. In the framework of improving the learning environment for SSE STEM subjects, in total 555 schools were supplied with mathematics tools; 134 schools with physics; 100 schools with chemistry; 82 schools with design-technology laboratory equipment; and 316 schools with audio-video sets. All 555 schools were officially registered in the Education Sector Information System (ESIS) as recipients of these equipment and tools. The regional trainings on the use of STEM education lab equipment, supplied by the project, was conducted in 6 aimags and 3 districts of Ulaanbaatar city in October and November 2020. In total 641 (70% female) physics, chemistry, and design & technology teachers, and the Education and Culture Department specialists in charge of science and technology education participated in the trainings. To increase the results of TV lessons that were launched due to the COVID-19 school lockdown, the teaching methodologies in 7 subjects (senor secondary math, science, and design & technology) were developed, and 4 subjects (math, chemistry, physics, and design & technology) teaching methodologies were printed out and distributed to teachers in 2020. Data Source: MES reports; M&E reports

Output: 4. Secondary education career guidance and advanced elective courses in science, technology, engineering, and math supported. Indicator: 90% of eighth and ninth grade teachers trained in gender sensitive career guidance Achievement: 100 Progress/Status: Achieved ahead of time and exceeded the target. The project engaged 4 person/months of international and 14 person/months of national consultancy services on junior and senior secondary education career guidance. Two sets of career guidance materials (junior and senior secondary grade) developed and prepared that consists of workbooks for students, guidelines for teachers, parents and school principals; and printed and distributed in 2016 and 2018. The project prepared 25 national trainers in career guidance. The trainers conducted training sessions nationwide in 2016, 2018 and 2019 and trained 14,031 people (82% female) including class teachers and school principals, training managers and social workers. More than 90% of eighth and ninth grade class teachers as part of school learning and career guidance teams were trained from 2016 to 2019. The 10th-12th grade class teachers (of whom more than 80% were women) were also trained in 2018 and 2019. Data Source: MES reports; M&E reports

Output: 4. Secondary education career guidance and advanced elective courses in science, technology, engineering, and math supported. Indicator: of which 70% are female teachers Achievement: 82.8 Data Source: MEDS reports; M&E reports

Output: 1. Industry-driven TVET system established in the three priority sectors. Indicator: By 2017: Standards for 15 key occupations validated with employers, and industry and professional associations in the three priority sectors Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Achieved with delay in 2019. Standards for 15 key occupations in 3 priority sectors (construction, agriculture and road) have been approved by the National Council on VET and sector sub-councils. The TVET standards and CBT curriculum for 15 occupations in 3 priority sectors were approved by the order No. A/303 of the Minister of Labor and Social Protection in September 2019 and delivered to TVET providers for implementation. All 134 pictorial learning guides for 15 occupations have been printed at ADMON printing house (total number of copies > 48000) and E -learning books of pictorial learning guides in 2 formats have been delivered to TVET AIMC and disseminated to TVET schools via AIMC' distance learning platform. Each school has sent records of the received books. The deliverables have been checked and the payment for the printing house was cleared. Data Source: MLSP reports; standards submitted to sector subcouncils for approval M&E reports Baseline year: 2012 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2012 Baseline value: N Target year: 2017 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Output: 1. Industry-driven TVET system established in the three priority sectors. Indicator: By 2021: Assessment and certification centers established in collaboration with employers, and industry and professional associations in the three priority sectors Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Achieved. Assessment and certification at VET AIMC and three assessment and certification centers (ACC) for the priority sectors have been established in 2021. The ACCs were established next to the Nalaikh TVET provider (road), Bayan-Chandmani TVET provider (agriculture), and Ulaanbaatar Polytechnic College (construction). All ACCs were rehabilitated and equipped with the training equipment. Test items and assessment tools for the key occupations were validated and approved by VET AIMC in December 2019. However, assessment and certification at VET AIMC and at three sectoral ACCs have been delayed due to the COVID-19 restrictions and were conducted in Aug 2021. Data Source: MLSP reports; reports of assessment and certification centers M&E reports Baseline year: 2012 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2012 Baseline value: N Target year: 2021 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Output: 3. Training systems for TVET managers and teachers established in the three priority sectors. Indicator: TVS training programs for teachers developed and delivered for the key occupations at accredited training institutes in the priority sectors Achievement: N Progress/Status: On 15 August 2019, the short-term technical and vocational skills training (TVS) programs for TVET teachers of 13 occupations along with training manual/handbook were introduced to the MLSP TVET Department. The TVS dissemination training for TVET teachers from 14 professions took place during August 2-20, 2021 period. The methodologists from the TVET AC has conducted the trainings which were conducted in Nalaikh TVET (competency center), Bayamchandmani PC (competency center), UB Construction PC (competency center) and, Dornod PC and Selenge-Zuunkharaa PC. A total of 165 teachers have participated in the dissemination trainings which lasted 4 days per professions. The training material and manuals have been sent to teachers to receive their comment and feedback. In the near future, the manuals can be updated and printed as main teachers manual for selected professions. The 47 teacher trainers for the 14 professions have been assessed by the TVET AC assessment team according to the assessment and certification guidelines. Data Source: MLSP reports; reports of TVS training providers for teachers Baseline year: 2012 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2012 Baseline value: N Target year: 2021 Target value: Y Actual value: N

Output: 3. Training systems for TVET managers and teachers established in the three priority sectors. Indicator: Training program for managers on industry-driven TVET management developed and delivered Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Achieved. An international consulting firm TTT developed a training module and manual for training managers and methodologists on industry-driven TVET management, and delivered to the MLSP on 15 August 2019. The selection of the institution to develop and deliver this training program was done through open competitive selection. There were 5 applicants who expressed their interests, and the University of Finance and Economics (jointly with and Dale Carnegie Center) was selected to deliver the training. A 2-stage training for TVET managers took place in February and June 2019 for 53 principals including 24 (44%) women from 36 TVET providers: (i) training conducted in February 2019; and (ii) training for the training managers conducted on 17-18 June 2019, delivered by the University of Finance and Economics. Data Source: MLSP reports Baseline year: 2012 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2012 Baseline value: N Target year: 2019 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Output: 4. Secondary education career guidance and advanced elective courses in science, technology, engineering, and math supported. Indicator: Eighth and ninth grade national instructional plan that integrates gender sensitive career guidance modules and materials implemented in all schools Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Achieved ahead of time and exceeded the target. Learning and career guidance for eight and ninth grade students has been implemented in all schools since 2016. Career guidance has been extended to 10th-12th grade students at all schools with 10th-12th grades since 2018. The career guidance activity has been included in the instructional plan approved by education ministers' orders No. A/103 in 2016 and No. A/491 in 2019. Learning and career guidance activities are being implemented as part of the extra-curricular activities during “school regulated hours”. Data Source: MES reports; M&E reports Baseline year: 2012 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2012 Baseline value: N Target year: 2020 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Output: 5. Effective project management system established. Indicator: Progress in achieving gender action plan targets monitored and reported Achievement: N Progress/Status: Out of total 12 activities of the GAP, 10 activities have been fully implemented, one is in-progress while one activity is not started. Average indicator status is 75.2%
Data Source: Quarterly and annual reports Baseline year: 2012 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2012 Baseline value: N Target year: 2019 Target value: Y Actual value: N

Output: 5. Effective project management system established. Indicator: Project performance management system established; baseline data collected (disaggregated by gender, income group, area, TVET provider or school, and occupation); and quarterly and annual reports generated Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Completed. The project performance management system was established in 2015, and the baseline data were collected in 2016. The quarterly and annual project progress reports are submitted generally on time. However, it was noted that the PIU have not been tracking and reflecting the progress against the performance targets/indicators in the PPMS; and the quarterly and annual progress report templates vary a lot and do not provide sufficient information about the project implementation. Data Source: Quarterly and annual reports Baseline year: 2012 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2012 Baseline value: N Target year: 2019 Target value: Y Actual value: Y
